html:
On 25 July 1261 a small army of the Empire of Nicaea under the general Alexios Strategopoulos took Constantinople back from the Latin Empire. The city had been in Latin hands for 57 years, since the sack of 1204.

Strategopoulos had only a few hundred soldiers and had been sent to watch the Bulgarian border. Near the city he learned from local Greeks that most of the Latin garrison and the Venetian fleet were away on a raid in the Black Sea. His men got in at night, with help from inside, and opened a gate. The Latin emperor Baldwin II fled in panic, leaving behind his crown and sceptre.

Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos made his solemn entry on 15 August and was crowned again in Hagia Sophia. The Byzantine Empire was restored, but the city was half empty and the empire much smaller and poorer than before 1204.
